description: Limits. A case with a `limits` object is decoded with those limits and not the defaults of 2 GiB and 10,000,000 entries, so a case need not be 2 GiB. `max_bytes` and `max_entries` are decimal strings. A manifest at the limit is accepted and one past it is refused, and the bytes are counted before anything is read.

cases.name: two entries with a limit of exactly two
the empty manifest with a limit of exactly 3 bytes
one byte over the byte limit
cases.reason: the manifest is longer than max_bytes, which is checked before any byte is read

cases.name: bytes that are no manifest at all, over the byte limit
cases.reason: the byte limit answers first, so the garbage is never parsed

cases.name: three entries with a limit of two
cases.reason: the entry count is over max_entries

cases.name: a count over the limit and no entry after it
cases.reason: the count alone decides: nothing follows it, and the entry limit is checked before the first entry

cases.name: the default entry limit: 10,000,001 entries
cases.reason: over 10,000,000, the default max_entries, with no limits object

cases.name: a count of 2^64 - 1
cases.reason: a count that no receiver reserves memory for

cases.name: a count the bytes cannot hold, under the default limit
cases.reason: the manifest ends before the entries it promises

cases.name: a pack count the bytes cannot hold
cases.reason: the pack list promises more packs than the bytes hold
